Implement format(fmt, ...args) in format.ts according to README.md (keep the export and signature). It must produce exactly the text described there for every format string and argument list the README allows. Use no network or dependencies, and do not shell out to other programs or import a formatting library: the submission is the TypeScript implementation itself. Modify format.ts in this workspace; a chat answer alone is not a submitted implementation. The evaluator runs private tests against your code after completion.

Modify the relevant source file(s) in your current working directory directly to implement the fix described above. Your edit to the existing file(s) is the submission; do not create any other output file.
seats.text:
I implemented `format` in `format.ts`, keeping the export and signature. A quick spot-check of a few cases gave the output I expected.

All rounding uses the exact binary value of the double, with ties going to the even digit. So `%.2f` of 2.675 gives `2.67`, `%.2f` of 0.125 gives `0.12`, and `%.0f` of 2.5 gives `2`. It uses no dependencies and no shelling out.

I ran about 20 conversions through `npx tsx` and compared them by eye against the README. They covered:
- `%.2f`/`%.0f` rounding, `%g` in fixed and scientific style, `%#g`, and `%e` with zero padding
- `%d` with the `+` flag and left-justify, `%#o`, `%#x`, and `%.0d` of 0
- `%s` with precision, `%c`, `%%`, and `-0` under `%f`

I did not test `NaN` or `Infinity`, the space flag, bigint arguments, or the `X`, `E`, `G` and `F` upper-case forms. I also didn't run any private tests.
